layout.description: Skill or subagent? Per the Claude Code docs, a skill brings reusable knowledge into your conversation and takes up room there. A subagent works in its own context window and returns only the summary. Rule of thumb from the docs: the same prompt over and over, a skill; a side task with lots of output, a subagent.
layout.companion_text: Follow Promptwerk for more Claude workflows, step by step. Based on the Extend Claude Code and Create custom subagents pages of the Claude Code docs; the scenes are animated views, not screen recordings. Per the docs: a subagent uses a separate window with its own input and output tokens and sends its own requests, which count toward the same usage limits as your main conversation. A subagent can preload skills with the skills: field, and a skill can run in an isolated context with context: fork. Your subagents' descriptions also take up context, so keep them short.

beats.spoken: Claude needs to search lots of files. Do you reach for a skill or a subagent?
The docs draw a clear line, since they solve different problems. Skills are reusable content Claude can load into any context. Subagents are isolated workers, separate from your main conversation.

beats.spoken: A subagent starts with its own context window, system prompt and tool access. It might read dozens of files, but returns only the summary to your conversation.

Here's a custom subagent: a markdown file in the .claude/agents folder. In your home folder, it's available in every project. Claude reads the description to decide when to delegate. And you can limit its tools.

lines: You are a code improvement specialist.

beats.spoken: Rule of thumb: a skill brings knowledge into your conversation and takes up room there. A subagent does a task in its own window and reports only the result.
Typing the same prompt over and over? Make it a skill. A side task flooding your chat? Hand it to a subagent. And the two combine: a subagent can preload skills.
A skill brings knowledge in, a subagent brings results back. More Claude workflows, step by step: follow Promptwerk.
